subject.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents

question: Should explicit `claws add --yes --plan-integrity` consent authorize installation or reuse of a process-wide shared plugin for an experimental Claw, or must the lifecycle wait for a separate host-level grant or per-agent plugin boundary?
rationale: This is a product and security-boundary choice: the implementation can bind a user to exact bytes and an exact action, but it cannot determine whether that consent appropriately authorizes a change visible to every agent in the runtime.

options.title: Accept exact-plan shared-host consent
options.body: Keep plugins process-wide for experimental v1, but require real proof of install/reuse and compensation before merge.

options.title: Require a separate host grant
options.body: Keep skill installation in this slice and defer shared-plugin mutation until a distinct host-level authorization flow is designed.

options.title: Defer plugin packages
options.body: Pause this package-owner slice until per-agent plugin isolation or a broader RFC decision supplies the intended boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept exact-plan shared-host consent
recommendation.body: Keep plugins process-wide for experimental v1, but require real proof of install/reuse and compensation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review comment directly identifies the agent-versus-shared-host authorization boundary that needs a maintainer decision.
